At a glance

What is Metre?

Metre is an AR tape measure for iPhone and iPad that measures length, height, area, volume, angles and whole homes with the camera, and shows a margin of error with every result.

Platforms
iPhone and iPad, iOS 17.0 or later, 36 languages, metric and imperial units.
LiDAR
Not required. Every tool except the automatic 3D room scan works without it; 3D room scan needs an iPhone or iPad Pro with LiDAR.
Price
Free to download, but Metre needs Metre Pro to measure; there is no free tier. Metre Pro is a weekly or monthly subscription (the monthly plan starts with a 3-day free trial), or a one-time lifetime purchase. It includes every tool, all 50 how-to demos, saving and every export.
Accuracy
Results are estimates. Every result shows a margin of error (± cm or in) and a quality label, and no camera-only phone is millimetre-exact.
Privacy
No account, no ads, no tracking. Camera images and photos are processed on the device. App Store privacy label: Data Not Collected.
Export
All exports are part of Metre Pro: PDF and CSV for saved projects, a listing PDF from the Home survey, and DXF and USDZ from LiDAR 3D room scans only.
Publisher
gokchetech, an independent developer.
What it measures

One app for the tape, the ruler, the level and the floor plan

Start with a quick length. Grow into a whole apartment, a kitchen wall or a tailor’s client book. Each tool explains itself with a short demo the first time you open it.

Smart scan

Aim at a table, a window, a door, a garment laid flat or a shoe. Metre outlines the object and reads its width × height, with no corners to tap. The result is an estimate, shown with its margin of error.

Length & height

Tap two points, or let them snap to edges and lines. Measure doors, shelves and ceilings, or a person’s height, found automatically from their body and the floor.

Area, box, angle & circle

Floors, walls and tabletops in m² or ft², parcels and appliances with volume, corners in degrees, and round tables, rugs or pipes.

Whole-home survey

Measure room by room. Metre adds up m² and m³, keeps net and total area apart, draws a bird’s-eye floor plan and exports a PDF.

LiDAR

3D room scan

On iPhone and iPad models with LiDAR, walk around a room and get its walls, doors, windows and floor plan. Export the scan as a USDZ 3D model, a DXF drawing for CAD or a PDF.

Will it fit? & Door check

Type the size from a shop listing and place a true-size virtual box in your room. Check the door opening before the delivery arrives.

Project calculators

Windows & curtains, paint, flooring and wallpaper, concrete in m³ and bags, tiles with adhesive and grout, stairs, slope, and a kitchen planner.

Body & tailor

Body measurements with a client measurement book for tailors, plus an approximate size estimate from a photo.

Ring, shoe & child height

Ring sizer with US, UK, EU and JP sizes, shoe size from foot length (EU, UK, US), and a child height tracker with dated history.

Ruler & level

A real-size on-screen ruler, calibrated once with any bank card, plus a bubble level and plumb.

Measure a photo

Pick a photo with a bank card or an A4 sheet in it and measure anything lying in the same plane.

Also: metric and imperial units (mm to yards, fractional inches), home-screen widgets, Siri Shortcuts, light and dark mode, and 36 languages.

Honest about accuracy

It tells you when to trust a number

A ring that shows confidence

The precision ring at the centre of the screen turns green when a point is reliable. Every result shows a margin of error (± cm or in) and a quality label: Accurate, Good or Approx.

Test your own phone in 20 seconds

Measure an A4 sheet or a bank card. Metre compares the result with the real size and shows how far off your phone is in this light, at this distance.

LiDAR helps, but isn’t required

Every tool except 3D room scan works with the camera alone. On LiDAR devices, surfaces are found faster, dim rooms work better, and 3D room scan becomes available.

Measurements are estimates. Before you cut, order or build, confirm critical dimensions with a physical tape.

Private by design

What the camera sees stays on your iPhone

Metre does its work on your device with Apple’s ARKit, Vision and RoomPlan. There is no Metre server to send anything to.

Read the privacy policy

  • Camera frames and photos are processed on the device and never uploaded.
  • No account, no sign-in, no email address needed.
  • No analytics, advertising or tracking code inside the app.
  • Your measurements are stored in the app on your device, and you can delete them at any time.

All how-to guides

Questions people ask

Measuring with a phone: straight answers

What is the best app to measure a room with an iPhone?

For a single distance, any AR tape measure will do, including Apple’s built-in Measure app. For a whole room you need more: floor area, perimeter, ceiling height, a floor plan you can share, and totals across several rooms.

That is what Metre’s Home survey is built for. Tap the corners of each room and it adds up m² or ft² and m³, draws a bird’s-eye floor plan and exports a PDF. On an iPhone or iPad with LiDAR, Metre can also create a 3D room scan with a floor plan automatically; a saved scan exports as a DXF drawing for CAD, a USDZ 3D model or a PDF. Both are part of Metre Pro.

Can my iPhone measure without LiDAR?

Yes. Every iPhone that runs iOS 17 supports ARKit, which combines the camera with the motion sensors to find floors, walls and tables and to measure between points. LiDAR, found on Pro iPhones since the iPhone 12 Pro and on iPad Pro models since 2020, adds a depth sensor: surfaces are found faster, dim rooms work better and results are usually more consistent.

In Metre every tool works without LiDAR except the automatic 3D room scan, because Apple’s RoomPlan requires a LiDAR scanner.

How accurate is an iPhone tape measure?

A phone gives an estimate, not a calibrated reading, and no camera-only phone is millimetre-exact. How close a result gets depends on the light, the surface, the distance and how steadily you hold the phone. An iPhone or iPad with a LiDAR scanner finds surfaces faster and usually more reliably than one without. Errors grow in dim light, on glass, mirrors, plain white walls and black fabric, at long distances and near the edge of the frame.

Metre does not hide this. Every result shows a margin of error (± cm or in) and a quality label, a precision ring turns green when it is confident, and Settings has a 20-second accuracy check: measure an A4 or Letter sheet and see how far off your own phone is in your own light. For cutting, ordering glass or anything you cannot undo, confirm with a physical tape.

How do I measure a window for curtains?

Measure the window’s width (the frame, or the recess if the curtains hang inside it) and its height. Then:

  • Rod length = window width + an overhang on each side, commonly 15 cm (6 in).
  • Fix the rod about 10–15 cm (4–6 in) above the window.
  • Curtain width = rod length × fullness: about 2× for gathered curtains, 1.5× for a lighter look.
  • Drop = from the rod to the sill, below the sill, or to the floor minus about 1 cm so the hem does not drag.

Metre’s Windows & curtains tool (part of Metre Pro) measures the window in AR and does this arithmetic for you.

How can I find my ring size with my phone?

The most reliable way is to measure a ring that already fits. Lay it on the screen and match a circle to its inside edge; the inside diameter converts to a size, for example 17.3 mm is about US 7, UK N½, EU 54.5.

Because screens differ, calibrate first. Metre’s Ring sizer (part of Metre Pro) uses a one-time calibration with a standard bank card (85.6 mm wide) and shows US, UK, EU and JP sizes. Measure at room temperature; if you are between two sizes, choose the larger one for wide bands.

How do I measure someone’s height with an iPhone?

Have the person stand straight with their feet visible, step back two or three metres and keep the whole body in the frame. Metre’s Height tool detects the body and the floor and measures automatically. The same tool measures doors, shelves and ceilings from two points. For children, the Height tracker (part of Metre Pro) keeps a dated history on your device.

How do I calculate the floor area of a room or apartment?

For a rectangular room, multiply length by width. For an L-shaped room, split it into rectangles and add them up. For an apartment, add up the rooms, and decide whether balconies count; they are usually left out of the net living area.

Metre’s Home survey (part of Metre Pro) lets you tap the corners of each room, choose the room type, keep net and total area apart, and export a floor plan as PDF.

Will this sofa fit, and will it go through the door?

Measure the space (width, depth, and the height under windows or shelves), then the door opening and any tight turns in the hallway. As a rule of thumb, a piece of furniture passes a door if its smallest dimension, often the depth, is less than the door’s clear width.

Metre’s Will it fit? places a true-size virtual box in your room from the dimensions in the shop listing, and Door check measures the opening for you. Both are part of Metre Pro.

Does Metre upload my photos or need an account?

No. Camera frames and photos are processed on your device with Apple’s ARKit, Vision and RoomPlan frameworks and are never uploaded. There is no account, no sign-in, no analytics, no ads and no tracking. Your measurements are stored in the app on your device.

Is Metre free?

Metre is free to download, but it needs Metre Pro to measure; there is no free tier. The monthly plan starts with a 3-day free trial and you can cancel anytime. A weekly plan (no trial) and a one-time lifetime purchase are also available.

Metre Pro includes every tool (length, height, level, the on-screen ruler, Smart scan, area, box and volume, the whole-home survey, 3D room scan, the calculators, the body and size tools), all 50 how-to demos, saving, and exports: PDF and CSV, plus DXF and USDZ from 3D room scans (LiDAR).
